To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) the best generalization performance is achieved in models that are locally smooth, but globally connected; and 2) the loss landscape is more globally connected when models are trained on larger datasets, and/or are trained with a larger model, and/or when they are trained on higher quality data.

1. The global connectivity of the loss landscape (i.e. the extent of its well-connected regions) correlates with test accuracy, and that 2. the local smoothness of the landscape correlates with test accuracy

(i) global connectivity of the loss landscape is a key factor in generalization performance; (ii) global connectivity is influenced by model size and data quantity; (iii) the best models have locally smooth regions; (iv) the best models are similar to each other, as measured by ensembles.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the relationship between the local geometry of the loss landscape and the global generalization properties of neural networks, and the factors that influence this relationship.
the question: What is the relationship between local and global structure in neural networks?

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the loss landscape of a trained neural network model is not a single, static, well-defined object, but rather a dynamic and evolving entity, which can vary in many ways depending on the task, model, training procedure, and data.

the loss landscape can be globally well- or poorly-connected, but the former correlates with better test accuracy; and that local landscape smoothness correlates with good test accuracy, but only when the loss landscape is already globally well-connected.
local metrics are more predictive of generalization performance than global metrics, but that global metrics are also important.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, while local structure is a useful proxy for global structure, there are also important aspects of global structure that cannot be captured by local measures.
the loss landscape structure can be taxonomized by the global versus local structure of the loss landscape.
the best test performance is achieved by models that have a loss landscape that is globally well-connected, and that is locally smooth.
The main takeaway from our work is that
local and global aspects of the loss landscapes are intertwined, and the best generalization performance is obtained in models where local and global aspects are well-aligned.
local and global metrics of the loss landscape are not independent, but rather that local metrics are more predictive of generalization performance than are global metrics.
the loss landscape structure can be a powerful tool for understanding the generalization behavior of neural network models.
